elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Section 7.4 as rendered still caps inspections at "no more than once each Calendar Year", which is a fixed January–December window rather than "any 12-month period" (audits in December and the following January would both be permitted); Section 4.9(a) now says "no more than once per year" but the two rights operate independently, so Array can conduct one facility inspection and one records inspection in the same year.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Both amended clauses fix notice at "at least fifteen (15) days" (Section 4.9(a): "upon at least fifteen (15) days' written notice"; Section 7.4: "on at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice"), short of the 30-day preferred standard.
Section 4.9(a) retains "during normal business hours", but Section 7.4 still permits inspections "at reasonable times" only, with no business-hours limitation.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Section 7.4 requires an "independent certified public accounting firm ... reasonably acceptable to Ono", but Section 4.9(a) still permits "Array, and/or an authorized representative" to inspect — i.e., Array itself, not an independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The Auditor confidentiality undertaking appears only in Section 7.4 ("execute a reasonable confidentiality agreement prior to commencing any such inspection"); the Section 4.9(a) inspector is subject to no confidentiality condition in the rendered text.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site preference was added; Section 4.9(a) expressly contemplates on-site entry into "the relevant facilities of Ono and its Affiliates", and Section 7.4 is silent on location.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Section 7.4 as rendered shifts cost where underpayment exceeds "ten percent (10%)", not 5 percent.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: No prohibition on system access was inserted; Section 4.9(a) retains the right to "enter the relevant facilities" and "examine any internal procedures or records", with mandatory "necessary and reasonable assistance" from Ono.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Section 4.9(a) now reads "to enter, no more than once per year, the relevant facilities", and Section 7.4 retains "Such inspections may be made no more than once each Calendar Year" plus "no more than one inspection" per calendar quarter of records — each audit right is annually capped.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Section 4.9(a): "upon at least fifteen (15) days' written notice"; Section 7.4: "on at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice" — both former open-ended "reasonable notice" standards replaced with a fixed 15-day minimum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Section 7.4: "Inspections ... shall be at the expense of Array, unless a variation or error producing an underpayment in amounts payable exceeding ten percent (10%) of the amount paid ... is established" — the redacted [ * ] threshold is now fixed at exactly 10%.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: annual frequency cap (both Section 4.9(a) and Section 7.4), a fixed 15-day notice minimum in both audit rights, and Array bearing inspection cost unless underpayment exceeds ten percent (10%).

Preferred level is not reached: notice is 15 rather than 30 days, the cost-shift trigger is 10% rather than 5%, no off-site preference or no-system-access prohibition was added, Section 7.4 still allows inspection merely "at reasonable times" (no business-hours limit), and Section 4.9(a) still allows Array itself (not an independent, confidentiality-bound auditor) to inspect. These are preferred-only gaps and do not defeat position-completeness at the fallback.

Minimality holds: the only changes are the frequency insertion in Section 4.9(a), the two notice-standard substitutions, and quantifying the redacted underpayment threshold at 10%. Favourable existing language (independent Auditor, Ono acceptability, Auditor confidentiality agreement, one inspection per quarter, minimisation of business disruption, interest mechanic) is retained untouched, and no survival tails, expense clauses or procedures were added.

Intent is preserved: the amendments sit inside the existing sentences, leave no undefined term or dangling cross-reference (Section 4.7, Section 7.1 and the Auditor definition all survive), and create no contradiction between Section 4.9(a) and Section 7.4, which govern different inspection subjects.

Optional tightening if pushing further: if the drafter wants the preferred position, change 15 to 30 days, reduce the Section 7.4 threshold to five percent (5%), convert "once each Calendar Year" to "once in any twelve (12)-month period", add "during normal business hours" to Section 7.4, and require the Section 4.9(a) inspector to be an independent representative bound by a confidentiality undertaking with no direct access to Ono systems.
